name: Gitea
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Gitea is a lightweight, self-hosted Git service with issues, pull requests, packages and CI. The egg runs it with SQLite, and you finish the setup in the browser on the first visit.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Gitea: downloads the Gitea binary from dl.gitea.com and checks it against
# Gitea's checksum. Repositories, the database and settings are never
# touched, and the binary is only replaced once the new one checks out.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

get() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 "$@"; }
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Gitea has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

base=https://dl.gitea.com/gitea
latest=$(get "$base/version.json" | jq -r '.latest.version') || fail "dl.gitea.com can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
version="${VERSION:-latest}"
version="${version#v}"
[ "$version" = latest ] && version="$latest"
url="$base/$version/gitea-$version-linux-$arch"
sum=$(get "$url.sha256" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1) ||
    fail "Gitea has no version $version. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as $latest."

if [ -f gitea ] && [ "$(sha256sum gitea | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ]; then
    echo "Gitea $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Gitea $version"
    get -o gitea.xz.new "$url.xz"
    xz -dc gitea.xz.new > gitea.new
    rm -f gitea.xz.new
    [ "$(sha256sum gitea.new | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ] || { rm -f gitea.new; fail "The download didn't match Gitea's checksum. Reinstall to try again."; }
    chmod +x gitea.new
    mv -f gitea.new gitea
fi

mkdir -p custom/conf data
# Older eggs kept the settings in app.ini or custom/app.ini: move them to
# where Gitea looks, so the server keeps its setup.
if [ ! -f custom/conf/app.ini ]; then
    for old in app.ini custom/app.ini; do
        if [ -f "$old" ] && grep -q INSTALL_LOCK "$old"; then
            mv "$old" custom/conf/app.ini
            echo "Moved the settings from $old to custom/conf/app.ini."
            break
        fi
    done
fi
# A first configuration: SQLite, logs on the console. The owner finishes
# the setup on the first visit (admin account, site name, address), which
# Gitea then saves here. Ports are kept up to date at every start.
if [ ! -f custom/conf/app.ini ]; then
    root_url=""
    case "${SERVER_IP:-}" in
        ""|0.0.0.0|127.0.0.1) ;;
        *) root_url="ROOT_URL = http://${SERVER_IP}:${SERVER_PORT}/" ;;
    esac
    cat > custom/conf/app.ini <<INI
Gitea_NAME = Gitea
RUN_MODE = prod
WORK_PATH = /home/container

[server]
PROTOCOL = http
HTTP_ADDR = 0.0.0.0
HTTP_PORT = ${SERVER_PORT:-3000}
${root_url}
START_SSH_SERVER = true
BUILTIN_SSH_SERVER_USER = git
SSH_PORT = ${SSH_PORT:-2020}
SSH_LISTEN_PORT = ${SSH_PORT:-2020}
DISABLE_SSH = ${DISABLE_SSH:-true}
Gitea_DATA_PATH = /home/container/data
LFS_START_SERVER = true

[database]
DB_TYPE = sqlite3
PATH = /home/container/data/gitea.db

[repository]
ROOT = /home/container/data/repositories

[log]
MODE = console
LEVEL = info
ROOT_PATH = /home/container/log

[security]
INSTALL_LOCK = false
INI
    echo "Wrote a first configuration. Open the server's address to finish setting Gitea up."
fi
echo "Installed Gitea $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Gitea version to install, such as 1.27.3, or latest.

variables.name: Disable SSH
variables.description: Set it to false to clone and push over SSH as well as HTTP. SSH needs its own port, added to the server first.

variables.name: SSH port
variables.description: The port Gitea's own SSH server listens on and shows in clone links, when SSH is on.
